steps.title: Understand the whole question
steps.body: Который час? — What time is it? This fixed question asks for the current clock time. The noun час normally means hour; its retained example label time reflects this question context rather than a universal translation of the isolated noun. Learn the complete question as a unit.

steps.title: Work the meaning choice
steps.body: For the complete clock question, choose What time is it? A question about which book someone wants would request a different kind of information. Repeated recognition of this one question is not independent practice in giving a time, asking when an event occurs, or forming other questions.

steps.title: Read the full question and the requested information
steps.body: Forms of который do not by themselves identify a clock question. Read the complete supplied question and its noun. Которое яблоко моё? — Which apple is mine? Asks which apple belongs to the speaker. This is the guided ownership/selection example. Которую книгу вы хотите? — Which book do you want? Asks which book the listener wants. The listener is asked to choose a book. Который час? — What time is it? Asks for the current clock time. This requests the current clock time, not which book the listener wants or which apple belongs to the speaker. The independent clock and book cues are different complete questions from the guided apple cue. These checks recognize the supplied meanings; they do not demonstrate independently asking/giving a new time or forming every interrogative. Optional repeated clock gloss practice is separate from the required checks.

The primary meaning is simply 'which one?', though '''которы
nativeSelections.originalSourceText:
=== Который? ===
The primary meaning is simply 'which one?', though '''который''' is also used to ask about one particular thing in a sequence of similar things.
:Which apple is mine? - '''Которое яблоко моё?'''
:What time is it? - '''Который час?'''
:Which book do you want? - '''Которую книгу вы хотите?'''
